name: login_elopage_buys
description: Purchases reported by the Elopage webhook. Nothing in gradido reads them except the question 'has this email bought anything', which is what user.hasElopage answers.

columns.name: elopage_user_id
columns.note: An Elopage number, external to gradido — not a gradido row identifier.

columns.name: publisher_id
columns.note: External Elopage number. The same publisher id users.publisher_id carries.

columns.name: product_price
columns.open: Legacy stores a price as a bare int with no unit and no currency. It is not a gradido amount and must not be read as one. What it counts has to be established from the Elopage side before anything computes with it.

columns.name: payer_email
columns.description: The only column anything reads: hasElopage counts rows matching a member's email.

columns.name: payed
columns.note: Spelled 'payed' in legacy. Names are stable forever — see contracts/AGENTS.md — so it stays as it is.

columns.name: event
columns.description: The webhook event name as Elopage sent it.

notes: This is inbound data from a foreign system, kept as it arrived. gradido derives one boolean from it and nothing else.
The lookup is by payer_email and there is no index on it. Legacy scans the table for every hasElopage call.
payer_email and publisher_email are personal data belonging to a third party's records. They are not login contacts and must never be joined into a user-facing response.

Legacy's collation on the two email columns is utf8_bin — case sensitive, unlike every other string column here. An implementation that compares emails case-insensitively will find rows legacy does not, and the answer to hasElopage changes.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. Legacy uses datetime without precision(3) — second precision.

open.question: Does this table survive into gradido2 at all?
open.detail: It exists for one boolean on one route. If the Elopage integration is not carried over, the table and user.hasElopage go together; if it is, the column widths and the missing index on payer_email are worth fixing rather than transcribing.
open.status: unanswered — decide with the Elopage webhook, not separately
